To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we give the first non-trivail approximation algorithm for the directed Steiner tree problem.

for the Directed Steiner tree problem we give the first non-trival approximation algorithm, and for the Directed generalized Steiner tree problem our algorithm achieves a non-trivial approximation ratio.

the Directed Steiner tree problem can be approximated within O(k^\epsilon), and the Directed Group Steiner tree, Node weighted Steiner tree, and Directed Generalized Stener tree problems can be approximated with a constant factor, for any fixed \epsilon > 0, in time O(k n^{1/\epsilon}).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient and non-trivial approximation schemes for a number of fundamental problems in the theory of directed graphs.
the design of approximation algorithms for NP-hard optimization problems. In particular, we are interested in the following questions.
the following two problems in directed graphs: Directed Steiner Tree Problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the directed versions of all these problems have been approximated within a constant factor.
the Directed Steiner problem has been solved.

we have the first non-trival approximations for the following directed Steiner problems: the Steiner tree problem in general directed graph, the generalized Steiner tree problem (with arbitrary edge costs and terminal demands) in general directed graph and the group Steiner tree problem on general directed graphs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we obtain the first nontrivial approximation algorithms for a wide class of directed Steiner tree problems.
we obtain the first non-constant approximations to the Directed Steiner problem in general digraphs.

we give the first approximation algorithms for the Directed Steiner tree problem with an approximation ratio of o(n^{0.5}) and the first o(n^{0}) approximation algorithm for the Generalized Stener tree problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Steiner Tree problems can be approximated in directed graphs, even when the number of terminals is not fixed.
the Directed Steiner tree problem is easier to solve than the Undirected Steiner tree problem.

the Steiner Tree and Generalized Steiner tree problems in directed graphs can be approximated to within a polylogarithmic factor in time O(k^{O(1)}) for k terminals or terminal pairs, which is the first non-trival result for these problems.
